claim: The promiscuous activities of enzymes provide fertile ground for the evolution of new metabolic pathways.
source: The promiscuous activities of enzymes provide fertile ground for the evolution of new metabolic pathways.
evidence: This is a statement from the abstract that draws on established scientific understanding about enzyme promiscuity and pathway evolution.

claim: Deletion of all threonine deaminases generated a strain in which isoleucine biosynthesis was interrupted at the level of 2-ketobutyrate.
source: By deleting all threonine deaminases, we generated a strain in which isoleucine biosynthesis was interrupted at the level of 2-ketobutyrate.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the experimental design and its effect on the metabolic pathway.

claim: Under aerobic conditions, a novel 2-ketobutyrate biosynthesis pathway emerged based upon the promiscuous cleavage of O-succinyl-L-homoserine by cystathionine γ-synthase (MetB).
source: Incubation of this strain under aerobic conditions resulted in the emergence of a novel 2-ketobutyrate biosynthesis pathway based upon the promiscuous cleavage of O-succinyl-L-homoserine by cystathionine γ-synthase (MetB).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Under anaerobic conditions, pyruvate formate-lyase enabled 2-ketobutyrate biosynthesis from propionyl-CoA and formate.
source: Under anaerobic conditions, pyruvate formate-lyase enabled 2-ketobutyrate biosynthesis from propionyl-CoA and formate.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: The anaerobic route provides a substantial fraction of isoleucine in a wild-type strain when propionate is available in the medium.
source: Surprisingly, we found this anaerobic route to provide a substantial fraction of isoleucine in a wild-type strain when propionate is available in the medium.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by labeling experiments shown in Figure 9.

claim: Underground metabolism provides metabolic redundancy and flexibility which allow for the best use of environmental carbon sources.
source: This study demonstrates the selective advantage underground metabolism offers, providing metabolic redundancy and flexibility which allow for the best use of environmental carbon sources.
evidence: This is an interpretive conclusion drawn from the experimental findings presented in the study.

claim: According to the patchwork model, underground metabolism provides fertile ground for the evolution of new pathways.
source: The patchwork model suggests that novel metabolic pathways emerge from the promiscuous activities of enzymes participating in diverse metabolic processes (Lazcano and Miller, 1999; Jensen, 1976; Khersonsky and Tawfik, 2010; Noda-Garcia et al., 2018). According to this, underground metabolism – the network of metabolic conversions which are catalyzed as side reactions of enzymes that have evolved to support other activities (D'Ari and Casadesús, 1998) – provides fertile ground for the evolution of new pathways.
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior literature on the patchwork model and underground metabolism.

claim: About half of all underground reactions generate metabolites that already exist in the endogenous metabolic network, enabling the emergence of metabolic bypasses.
source: A computational analysis suggested that about half of all underground reactions generate metabolites that already exist in the endogenous metabolic network, thus enabling the emergence of metabolic bypasses for the production of key cellular building blocks (Notebaart et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a computational analysis by Notebaart et al., 2014.

claim: Promiscuous activities of arginine biosynthesis enzymes enabled proline production in an E. coli strain deleted in the canonical proline biosynthesis route.
source: For example, promiscuous activities of the arginine biosynthesis enzymes enabled proline production in an E. coli strain deleted in the canonical proline biosynthesis route (Itikawa et al., 1968)
evidence: This is an example from prior literature cited to support the concept of underground metabolism.

claim: Several pathways based on promiscuous activities of different enzymes have been shown to relieve pyridoxal phosphate auxotrophy in E. coli.
source: several pathways, each based on the promiscuous activities of different enzymes, have been shown to relieve pyridoxal phosphate auxotrophy in E. coli (Kim et al., 2010; Oberhardt et al., 2016)
evidence: This is an example from prior literature cited to support the concept of underground metabolism.

claim: Adaptive evolution of E. coli harnessed enzyme promiscuity to enable growth on 1,2-propanediol.
source: and adaptive evolution of E. coli harnessed enzyme promiscuity to enable growth on the non-natural feedstock 1,2-propanediol (Lee and Palsson, 2010).
evidence: This is an example from prior literature cited to support the concept of underground metabolism.

claim: Cellular production of isoleucine and valine are catalyzed by the same enzymes.
source: Cellular production of isoleucine and valine are catalyzed by the same enzymes
evidence: This is a statement of established biochemical knowledge about branched-chain amino acid biosynthesis.

claim: In valine biosynthesis, pyruvate is self-condensed whereas in isoleucine biosynthesis, pyruvate is condensed with 2-ketobutyrate.
source: in valine biosynthesis, pyruvate is self-condensed whereas in isoleucine biosynthesis, pyruvate is condensed with 2-ketobutyrate (2 KB).
evidence: This is a statement of established biochemical knowledge about the differences between valine and isoleucine biosynthesis.

claim: In most organisms, 2 KB is produced from threonine cleavage.
source: In most organisms, 2 KB is produced from threonine cleavage.
evidence: This is a statement of established biochemical knowledge about the canonical 2-ketobutyrate biosynthesis pathway.

claim: The citramalate route mirrors the TCA cycle, where pyruvate is condensed with acetyl-CoA, and 2 KB is the pathway product.
source: For example, the citramalate route mirrors the TCA cycle, where pyruvate, rather than oxaloacetate, is condensed with acetyl-CoA, and 2 KB, rather than 2-ketoglutarate, is the pathway product (Charon et al., 1974).
evidence: This is a statement about an alternative 2-ketobutyrate biosynthesis pathway supported by a citation.

claim: In several anaerobic microorganisms, propionate is converted to 2 KB in a reductive pathway that mirrors acetate conversion to pyruvate.
source: Similarly, in several anaerobic microorganisms, propionate is converted to 2 KB in a reductive pathway that mirrors acetate conversion to pyruvate via ligation with CoA and ferredoxin-dependent carboxylation (Buchanan, 1969; Monticello et al., 1984; Eikmanns et al., 1983).
evidence: This is a statement about an alternative 2-ketobutyrate biosynthesis pathway supported by citations.

claim: In plants, methionine γ-lyase is a complementary source of cellular 2 KB.
source: In plants, methionine γ-lyase, catalyzing a reaction similar to that of cystathionine γ-lyase, is a complementary source of cellular 2 KB (Joshi and Jander, 2009; Joshi et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a statement about an alternative 2-ketobutyrate biosynthesis pathway in plants supported by citations.

claim: The ΔilvA ΔtdcB strain grew identically to the WT strain when provided with isoleucine.
source: When provided with isoleucine, this strain grew identically to the WT strain (dark red line in Figure 2).
evidence: This is a direct observation from growth experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: Without the addition of isoleucine, the ΔilvA ΔtdcB strain showed no growth in the first 70 hr, but within 70–120 hr, different replicates started growing.
source: Without the addition of isoleucine, we observed no growth in the first 70 hr, but within 70–120 hr, different replicates started growing with a growth rate somewhat lower than that of the WT strain (purple lines in Figure 2).
evidence: This is a direct observation from growth experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: Serine deaminases are known to accept threonine as a substrate.
source: One explanation of the observed growth without isoleucine is an increased activity of serine deaminases, which are known to accept threonine as a substrate (Cicchillo et al., 2004).
evidence: This is a statement of established biochemical knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Strain Δ5 (ΔilvA ΔtdcB ΔsdaA ΔsdaB ΔtdcG) displayed similar behavior to the ΔilvA ΔtdcB strain, with growth starting after 70 hr without isoleucine.
source: However, strain Δ5 displayed similar behavior to the ΔilvA ΔtdcB strain, that is, while growth without isoleucine was not observed in the first 70 hr, after 70 hr, the replicates started growing (green lines in Figure 2).
evidence: This is a direct observation from growth experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: The similar growth behavior of Δ5 and ΔilvA ΔtdcB strains strongly suggests the emergence of a latent threonine-independent isoleucine biosynthesis pathway.
source: This strongly suggests the emergence of a latent threonine-independent isoleucine biosynthesis pathway.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that deleting serine deaminases did not prevent growth without isoleucine.

claim: The ΔilvC strain could not grow without isoleucine even after 150 hr.
source: While cultivation of the ΔilvC strain with valine and isoleucine enabled growth similar to that of the WT strain (pink line in Figure 2; valine is required as IlvC participates also in valine biosynthesis), growth without isoleucine was not observed even after 150 hr (orange line in Figure 2).
evidence: This is a direct observation from growth experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: Addition of 2 KB to the cultivation medium rescued the growth of the ΔilvA ΔtdcB strain and the Δ5 strain but not the ΔilvC strain.
source: As a further confirmation, we observed that addition of 2 KB to the cultivation medium rescued the growth of the ΔilvA ΔtdcB strain and the Δ5 strain but not the ΔilvC strain (Figure 2).
evidence: This is a direct observation from growth experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: 2 KB serves as a metabolic intermediate in the underground isoleucine biosynthesis pathway.
source: This confirms that 2 KB still serves as a metabolic intermediate in the underground isoleucine biosynthesis pathway.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that ΔilvC cannot grow without isoleucine but can grow with 2 KB supplementation.

claim: The labeling pattern of isoleucine in the ΔilvA ΔtdcB and the Δ5 strains is almost identical to that of the WT strain.
source: The labeling pattern of isoleucine in the ΔilvA ΔtdcB and the Δ5 strains is almost identical to that of the WT strain (Figure 3B, the small deviations from the expected labeling can be attributed to the ambient abundance of 13C and the shuffling of labeled carbon by the activity of the pentose phosphate pathway and the TCA cycle).
evidence: This is a direct observation from isotope labeling experiments shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The labeling pattern effectively rules out the activity of the citramalate pathway for 2 KB biosynthesis in the mutant strains.
source: This effectively rules out the activity of the citramalate pathway and indicates that the biosynthesis of 2 KB in both gene deletion strains is closely related to the natural production pathway.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the isotope labeling data showing that the labeling pattern does not match what would be expected from the citramalate pathway.

claim: The Δ5 ΔmetA strain could not grow without isoleucine.
source: The Δ5 ΔmetA strain could grow with the addition of methionine and isoleucine (Figure 4, pink line), while no growth was observed without isoleucine (Figure 4, orange line).
evidence: This is a direct observation from growth experiments shown in Figure 4.

claim: The production of 2 KB in the Δ5 strain is dependent on the methionine biosynthesis route.
source: This indicates that the production of 2 KB in the Δ5 strain is indeed dependent on the methionine biosynthesis route.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that deleting metA prevents growth without isoleucine.

claim: In E. coli, cystathionine undergoes β-elimination which generates homocysteine and pyruvate, not γ-elimination.
source: Specifically, in this bacterium, cystathionine does not undergo γ-elimination but rather β-elimination which generates homocysteine and pyruvate (Figge, 2006).
evidence: This is a statement of established biochemical knowledge about E. coli metabolism supported by a citation.

claim: E. coli lacks a characterized annotated methionine γ-lyase.
source: Also, E. coli lacks a characterized annotated methionine γ-lyase.
evidence: This is a statement about the absence of a specific enzyme in E. coli based on genomic annotation.

claim: The inability of the Δ5 ΔmetA strain to grow when supplemented with methionine but not isoleucine confirms that E. coli lacks methionine γ-lyase activity.
source: While an E. coli gene was previously suggested to encode for such an enzyme (Manukhov et al., 2005), the inability of the Δ5 ΔmetA strain to grow when supplemented with methionine but not isoleucine confirms that E. coli lacks methionine γ-lyase activity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the growth experiment with the Δ5 ΔmetA strain.

claim: MetB can cleave O-succinyl-L-homoserine to succinate and 2-ketobutyrate.
source: First, rather than catalyzing the condensation of cysteine with O-succinyl-L-homoserine, cystathionine γ-synthase (MetB) can cleave the latter intermediate to succinate and 2 KB (reaction one in Figure 5; kcat﻿﻿ = 7.7 s−1 and KM(O-succinyl-L-homoserine)=0.33 mM for E. coli enzyme [Figge, 2006; Holbrook et al., 1990]).
evidence: This is a statement about enzyme activity supported by citations to prior literature and confirmed by experiments in this study.

claim: MetB can condense O-succinyl-L-homoserine and homocysteine to give homolanthionine.
source: MetB can also condense O-succinyl-L-homoserine and homocysteine to give homolanthionine (reaction two in Figure 5; KM(homocysteine)=0.54 mM for C. glutamicum enzyme [Krömer et al., 2006])
evidence: This is a statement about enzyme activity supported by a citation to prior literature on the C. glutamicum enzyme.

claim: MetC can cleave homolanthionine to regenerate homocysteine and produce 2 KB.
source: which can be subsequently cleaved by cystathionine-β-lyase (MetC) to regenerate homocysteine and produce 2 KB (reaction three in Figure 5; e.g. kcat ≈ 180 s−1 and KM(homolanthionine)=4.5 mM for E. coli enzyme [Figge, 2006; Krömer et al., 2006; Alting et al., 1995; Dwivedi et al., 1982]).
evidence: This is a statement about enzyme activity supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: MetC from various organisms can catalyze both the β-elimination and the γ-elimination of cystathionine, giving rise to both pyruvate and 2 KB.
source: In addition, MetC from various organisms can catalyze both the β-elimination and the γ-elimination of cystathionine, giving rise to both pyruvate and 2 KB (reaction four in Figure 5; e.g. kcat(γ-elimination) ≈ 0.9 s−1 and KM(cystathionine)=0.20 mM for Streptomyces phaeochromogenes enzyme where β-elimination proceeds at ≈ 1/7 rate of γ-elimination [Alting et al., 1995; Nagasawa et al., 1984]).
evidence: This is a statement about enzyme activity in various organisms supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: MetC can cleave cysteine to pyruvate.
source: As MetC can also cleave cysteine to pyruvate (kcat ≈ 1.8 s−1 for E. coli enzyme [Dwivedi et al., 1982; Awano et al., 2003; Flint et al., 1996])
evidence: This is a statement about enzyme activity supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Some MetC variants can act as methionine γ-lyase, releasing 2 KB by directly cleaving methionine.
source: Finally, some MetC variants can act as methionine γ-lyase, releasing 2 KB by directly cleaving methionine (reaction six in Figure 5; e.g. kcat ≈ 0.01 s−1 for Lactococcus lactis subsp. cremoris B78 enzyme [Alting et al., 1995; Amarita et al., 2004; Irmler et al., 2008]).
evidence: This is a statement about enzyme activity in specific organisms supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: MetC from E. coli did not catalyze the degradation of cystathionine, homocysteine, or methionine to 2 KB.
source: We found that MetC from E. coli did not catalyze the degradation of cystathionine, homocysteine, or methionine to 2 KB (ruling out reactions 4, 5, and 6 in Figure 5).
evidence: This is a direct observation from enzymatic assays performed in this study.

claim: The Δ5 ΔmetC strain could grow even without the addition of methionine.
source: To further confirm that MetC is not involved in 2 KB production, we deleted its encoding gene. The Δ5 ΔmetC strain could grow even without the addition of methionine (which is in line with the ΔmetC strain in the Keio collection [Baba et al., 2006])
evidence: This is a direct observation from growth experiments and is consistent with prior literature.

claim: The Δ5 ΔmetC strain could directly grow without isoleucine and without the need for adaptation.
source: More importantly, this strain could directly grow without isoleucine and without the need for adaptation (green line in Figure 4).
evidence: This is a direct observation from growth experiments shown in Figure 4.

claim: MetB catalyzes the cleavage of O-succinyl-L-homoserine to 2 KB with kcat = 9.3 ± 0.4 s−1 and KM(O-succinyl-L-homoserine)=0.60 ± 0.08 mM.
source: Supporting previous studies (Figge, 2006; Holbrook et al., 1990), we found MetB to catalyze the cleavage of O-succinyl-L-homoserine to 2 KB (reaction one in Figure 5) with kcat = 9.3 ± 0.4 s−1, KM(O-succinyl-L-homoserine)=0.60 ± 0.08 mM, and thus kcat/KM(O-succinyl-L-homoserine)=16 ± 2 mM−1 s−1 (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is a direct measurement from enzymatic assays performed in this study, consistent with prior literature.

claim: Formation of 2 KB by MetB is suppressed in the presence of cysteine.
source: Yet, it was previously reported that the formation of 2 KB is suppressed in the presence of cysteine (Holbrook et al., 1990).
evidence: This is a statement from prior literature supported by a citation.

claim: Formation of 2 KB by MetB was suppressed at physiological concentrations of cysteine, while homocysteine suppressed 2 KB formation only at high concentrations.
source: We found that formation of 2 KB was indeed suppressed at physiological concentrations of cysteine, while homocysteine suppressed 2 KB formation only at high concentrations (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B–E).
evidence: This is a direct observation from enzymatic assays shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: Deletion of metB in the Δ5 strain completely abolishes growth without isoleucine.
source: Nonetheless, as the deletion of metB in the Δ5 strain completely abolishes growth without isoleucine (brown line in Figure 4), it seems very likely that MetB is involved in the production of 2 KB.
evidence: This is a direct observation from growth experiments shown in Figure 4.

claim: In most of the sequenced strains (11 out of 16), metC was either deleted or mutated.
source: We found that in most of the sequenced strains (11 strains out of the 16 sequenced) metC was either deleted or mutated (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a direct observation from whole-genome sequencing of evolved strains.

claim: A lower metabolic flux toward methionine biosynthesis enhances the side reactivity of the pathway enzymes and results in a higher conversion rate of O-succinyl-L-homoserine to 2 KB.
source: It therefore seems that a lower metabolic flux toward methionine biosynthesis, as expected by the deletion of metC, enhances the side reactivity of the pathway enzymes and results in a higher conversion rate of O-succinyl-L-homoserine to 2 KB.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that metC deletion enables immediate growth without isoleucine.

claim: In the Δ5 ΔmetC strain, the concentration of methionine was approximately 3-fold lower than in the WT strain and the Δ5 strain.
source: Indeed, we found that, as compared to the WT strain and the Δ5 strain, in the Δ5 ΔmetC strain the concentration of methionine was ≈3-fold lower (Figure 6A)
evidence: This is a direct measurement from metabolite quantification shown in Figure 6A.

claim: In the Δ5 ΔmetC strain, the concentration of O-succinyl-L-homoserine was approximately 3-fold higher than in the WT strain and the Δ5 strain.
source: while the concentration of O-succinyl-L-homoserine was ≈3-fold higher (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is a direct measurement from metabolite quantification shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Another mutated strain harbored a single mutation in the gene coding for serine acetyltransferase (CysE): Ala33Thr.
source: Another mutated strain harbored a single mutation in the gene coding for serine acetyltransferase (CysE): Ala33Thr (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a direct observation from whole-genome sequencing of evolved strains.

claim: The Δ5 cysE* strain grew immediately on a medium without isoleucine and with a growth rate identical to the WT strain.
source: The resulting strain (Δ5 cysE*) grew immediately (with no lag time) on a medium without isoleucine and with a growth rate identical to the WT strain (purple lines in Figure 4; note that the growth of the Δ5 cysE* strain was considerably faster than that of the Δ5 ΔmetC strain).
evidence: This is a direct observation from growth experiments shown in Figure 4.

claim: The Ala33Thr mutation in CysE decreased the apparent kcat of the enzyme 2-fold, from 350 ± 30 s−1 to 170 ± 30 s−1.
source: Despite the mutation occurring far from the active site, we found that the apparent kcat of the enzyme decreased 2-fold, from 350 ± 30 s−1 to 170 ± 30 s−1
evidence: This is a direct measurement from enzymatic assays performed in this study.

claim: The Ala33Thr mutation in CysE increased the KM for acetyl-CoA by more than 8-fold, from 0.6 ± 0.2 mM to 5.0 ± 2.0 mM.
source: while the KM for acetyl-CoA increased by more than 8-fold, from 0.6 ± 0.2 mM to 5.0 ± 2.0 mM
evidence: This is a direct measurement from enzymatic assays performed in this study.

claim: The concentration of acetyl-CoA in E. coli lies in the range of 0.6–0.75 mM.
source: As the concentration of acetyl-CoA in E. coli lies in the range of 0.6–0.75 mM (Bennett et al., 2009)
evidence: This is a statement about cellular metabolite concentrations supported by a citation.

claim: The Ala33Thr mutation is expected to decrease the rate of the CysE reaction by more than 17-fold under physiological conditions.
source: Overall, the Ala33Thr mutation is expected to decrease the rate of the CysE reaction by more than 17-fold under physiological conditions.
evidence: This is a calculation based on the measured kinetic parameters and known cellular metabolite concentrations.

claim: The decreased activity of CysE halved the intracellular cysteine concentration relative to that of the WT strain and the Δ5 strain.
source: The decreased activity of CysE halved the intracellular cysteine concentration relative to that of the WT strain and the Δ5 strain (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a direct measurement from metabolite quantification shown in Figure 7.

claim: The lower availability of cysteine led to more than a 2-fold reduction in methionine concentration in the Δ5 cysE* strain.
source: This deprived MetB of its co-substrate, thus lowering the methionine biosynthesis flux and resulting in more than a 2-fold reduction in methionine concentration (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is a direct measurement from metabolite quantification shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The lower availability of methionine led to overexpression of genes participating in its biosynthesis, increasing the transcript level of metA and metB more than 3-fold relative to the WT strain and the Δ5 strain.
source: The lower availability of methionine led to overexpression of genes participating in its biosynthesis, increasing the transcript level of metA and metB more than 3-fold relative to the WT strain and the Δ5 strain (Figure 6B; interestingly, such increase in transcript level was not observed in the Δ5 ΔmetC strain).
evidence: This is a direct measurement from RT-qPCR experiments shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The higher expression of MetA and MetB, coupled with partial lifting of MetA inhibition by methionine, led to a dramatic 30- to 60-fold increase in the concentration of O-succinyl-L-homoserine in the Δ5 cysE* strain.
source: This higher expression, as well as the partial lifting of MetA inhibition by methionine (Born and Blanchard, 1999), led to a dramatic 30- to 60-fold increase in the concentration of O-succinyl-L-homoserine (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is a direct measurement from metabolite quantification shown in Figure 6A, with an inference about MetA inhibition supported by a citation.

claim: The Δ5 strain failed to grow without the addition of isoleucine under anaerobic conditions, even after 120 hr.
source: However, we did not observe the reemergence of the metC deletion, the cysE* mutation, or any other mutation: the Δ5 strain failed to grow without the addition of isoleucine, even after 120 hr (black lines in Figure 8A).
evidence: This is a direct observation from anaerobic growth experiments shown in Figure 8A.

claim: PFL catalyzes the condensation of propionyl-CoA and formate to give 2 KB with a specific activity of 0.6–1.1 μmol/min/mg.
source: We indeed found that a purified PFL catalyzes the condensation of propionyl-CoA and formate to give 2 KB with a specific activity of 0.6–1.1 μmol/min/mg, kcat of 0.9–1.7 s−1, KM(propionyl-CoA)=0.83 ± 0.6 mM and KM(formate)=69 ± 11 mM (Table 1, Materials and methods, Figure 5—figure supplement 1, and Figure 8—figure supplements 2 and 3).
evidence: This is a direct measurement from enzymatic assays performed in this study.

claim: The Δ5 strain could grow anaerobically when propionate and formate were added to the medium instead of isoleucine.
source: We found that the Δ5 strain could grow anaerobically when propionate and formate were added to the medium instead of isoleucine (red line in Figure 8A).
evidence: This is a direct observation from anaerobic growth experiments shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Propionate alone, when added to the medium, supported the growth of the Δ5 strain anaerobically, albeit with longer lag time and lower growth rate than with the addition of formate.
source: Indeed, we found that propionate alone, when added to the medium, supported the growth of the Δ5 strain, albeit with longer lag time and lower growth rate than with the addition of formate (purple line in Figure 8A, all replicates displayed an identical growth phenotype, thus ruling out genetic mutations).
evidence: This is a direct observation from anaerobic growth experiments shown in Figure 8A.

claim: The Δ5 ΔpflB strain could not grow with propionate as isoleucine precursor, with or without further addition of formate.
source: However, replacement of isoleucine with propionate, with or without further addition of formate, resulted in no growth (red and purple lines in Figure 8B).
evidence: This is a direct observation from anaerobic growth experiments shown in Figure 8B.

claim: PFL is responsible for 2 KB biosynthesis from propionate under anaerobic conditions.
source: This confirms that PFL is indeed responsible for 2 KB biosynthesis.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that deleting pflB prevents growth with propionate as isoleucine precursor.

claim: In a WT strain under anaerobic conditions, the addition of labeled propionate resulted in 30% labeled isoleucine.
source: Surprisingly, we found that even within a WT strain, the addition of labeled propionate resulted in 30% labeled isoleucine (Figure 9)
evidence: This is a direct observation from isotope labeling experiments shown in Figure 9.

claim: The KBFL route operates naturally in WT E. coli if propionate is present in the medium under anaerobic conditions.
source: suggesting that the KBFL route operates naturally if propionate is present in the medium.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that labeled propionate leads to labeled isoleucine in WT cells.

claim: When formate was added to the medium along with labeled propionate, the fraction of labeled isoleucine increased to almost 60% in WT strain under anaerobic conditions.
source: When formate was also added to the medium, the fraction of labeled isoleucine increased to almost 60% (Figure 9), making the KBFL-dependent pathway the dominant isoleucine biosynthesis route within a WT strain.
evidence: This is a direct observation from isotope labeling experiments shown in Figure 9.

claim: In the Δ5 strain under anaerobic conditions, isoleucine was almost 80% labeled upon addition of formate and labeled propionate.
source: In the Δ5 strain, in which the canonical isoleucine biosynthesis pathways are deleted, isoleucine was almost 80% labeled upon addition of formate and labeled propionate (Figure 9).
evidence: This is a direct observation from isotope labeling experiments shown in Figure 9.

claim: Deletion of metA increased the labeling of isoleucine to 90% in the Δ5 strain under anaerobic conditions with labeled propionate and formate.
source: Deletion of the metA increased this labeling to 90% (Figure 9), indicating that the MetB-dependent route operates anaerobically although with a low flux.
evidence: This is a direct observation from isotope labeling experiments shown in Figure 9.

claim: There might be another undiscovered yet marginal route for isoleucine biosynthesis, as 10% of the isoleucine was not labeled even in the Δ5 ΔmetA strain.
source: As 10% of the isoleucine was not labeled even in the Δ5 ΔmetA strain, it seems that there might be another undiscovered yet marginal route for isoleucine biosynthesis.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the observation that some isoleucine remains unlabeled even when known pathways are blocked or labeled.

claim: TdcE catalyzes the condensation of propionyl-CoA and formate to give 2 KB with a specific activity of 1.8–2.1 μmol/min/mg.
source: We found that purified TdcE is catalytically superior to PFL, generating 2 KB with a specific activity of 1.8–2.1 μmol/min/mg, kcat of 2.7–3.2 s−1, KM(propionyl-CoA)=0.52 ± 0.08 mM, and KM(formate)=20 ± 3 mM (Table 1, Materials and methods, Figure 5—figure supplement 1, and Figure 8—figure supplements 2 and 3).
evidence: This is a direct measurement from enzymatic assays performed in this study.

claim: While the deletion of pflB abolished isoleucine labeling from propionate, deletion of tdcE resulted in identical labeling to that of the WT strain.
source: Yet, while the deletion of pflB (in which case acetate was further added to the medium) abolished isoleucine labeling, deletion of tdcE resulted in identical labeling to that of the WT strain (Figure 9).
evidence: This is a direct observation from isotope labeling experiments shown in Figure 9.

claim: PFL is solely responsible for the production of 2 KB from propionate and formate under the tested conditions.
source: This indicates that PFL is solely responsible for the production of 2 KB from propionate and formate.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that deleting pflB but not tdcE abolishes isoleucine labeling from propionate.

claim: Overexpression of tdcE in a Δ5 ΔpflB strain enabled fast growth with propionate.
source: We found that overexpression of tdcE in a Δ5 ΔpflB strain enabled fast growth with propionate (purple line in Figure 8C)
evidence: This is a direct observation from growth experiments shown in Figure 8C.

claim: TdcE can replace PFL both in catalyzing pyruvate cleavage to generate formate and in catalyzing 2 KB production from propionyl-CoA and formate.
source: indicating that TdcE can replace PFL both in catalyzing pyruvate cleavage to generate formate (as noted previously [Sawers et al., 1998]) and in catalyzing 2 KB production from propionyl-CoA and formate.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that overexpressing tdcE rescues growth of the ΔpflB strain with propionate.

claim: Overexpression of tdcE in a WT strain fed with propionate-1-13C resulted in more than 70% labeled isoleucine without externally added formate and ~90% with externally added formate.
source: Moreover, overexpression of tdcE in a WT strain fed with propionate-1-13C resulted in a high proportion of labeled isoleucine: more than 70% without externally added formate and ~90% with externally added formate, both are considerably higher than without tdcE overexpression (Figure 9).
evidence: This is a direct observation from isotope labeling experiments shown in Figure 9.

claim: Overexpression of tdcE in the Δ5 ΔmetA strain resulted in 95% labeled isoleucine, the highest labeling observed.
source: Overexpression of tdcE in the Δ5 ΔmetA strain resulted in 95% labeled isoleucine, the highest labeling we observed (Figure 9).
evidence: This is a direct observation from isotope labeling experiments shown in Figure 9.

claim: Underground metabolism provides metabolic redundancy and flexibility which allows for the best use of environmental carbon sources.
source: This study serves to demonstrate the selective advantage underground metabolism may offer in nature, providing metabolic redundancy and flexibility which allows for the best use of environmental carbon sources (Notebaart et al., 2014).
evidence: This is an interpretive conclusion drawn from the experimental findings, with a citation to support the concept.

claim: The aerobic pathway uncovered represents a classic case of underground metabolism where a promiscuous reaction is enhanced by rewiring cellular metabolism.
source: The first pathway, uncovered under aerobic conditions, is based on rerouting the metabolism of O-succinyl-L-homoserine from methionine biosynthesis toward the production of 2 KB. This represents a rather classic case of underground metabolism: a promiscuous reaction, the activity of which normally has a negligible physiological contribution, is enhanced by the rewiring of cellular metabolism under conditions which couple it to growth.
evidence: This is an interpretive conclusion drawn from the experimental findings about the aerobic pathway.

claim: A change in the steady-state concentration of cysteine greatly enhances the promiscuous activity of MetB and enables a new biosynthetic route.
source: Interestingly, a change in the steady-state concentration of a seemingly unrelated metabolite – cysteine – greatly enhances this promiscuous activity and enables a new biosynthetic route.
evidence: This is an interpretive conclusion drawn from the experimental findings about the cysE* mutation and its effects.

claim: The anaerobic KBFL pathway was highly active also in a WT strain, providing a substantial fraction of cellular isoleucine when propionate was present in the medium.
source: Under anaerobic conditions, we uncovered a pathway that relies on the highly expressed PFL (Neidhardt et al., 1996) to condense propionyl-CoA and formate to 2 KB. This route, unlike the aerobic cleavage of O-succinyl-L-homoserine, was highly active also in a WT strain, providing a substantial fraction of cellular isoleucine when propionate was present in the medium.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the isotope labeling experiments showing significant labeling in WT cells.

claim: Short-chain fatty acids, such as propionate, are abundant in the mammalian intestine, the native habitat of E. coli.
source: As short-chain fatty acids, such as propionate, are abundant in the mammalian intestine (McNeil et al., 1978), the native habitat of E. coli
evidence: This is a statement about the natural environment of E. coli supported by a citation.

claim: The KBFL pathway is likely to play a key role in isoleucine biosynthesis under physiological conditions in E. coli's native habitat.
source: the KBFL pathway is likely to play a key role in isoleucine biosynthesis under physiological conditions.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that the pathway is active in WT cells and propionate is abundant in E. coli's natural habitat.

claim: The KBFL pathway should be regarded as an auxiliary biosynthesis route based on promiscuous enzyme activities rather than underground metabolism.
source: Hence, this pathway does not actually represent underground metabolism, but rather should be regarded an auxiliary biosynthesis route based on promiscuous enzyme activities.
evidence: This is an interpretive conclusion about the classification of the KBFL pathway based on its activity in WT cells.

claim: The use of the KBFL pathway is favorable over the canonical threonine cleavage route as it better uses the carbon sources available in the environment.
source: The use of the KBFL pathway is favorable over the canonical threonine cleavage route as it better uses the carbon sources available in the environment.
evidence: This is an interpretive conclusion about the selective advantage of the KBFL pathway.

claim: PFL should be renamed 'pyruvate formate-lyase/2-ketobutyrate formate-lyase' to reflect its dual activity.
source: As PFL supports the KBFL reaction under physiological conditions, we suggest renaming it 'pyruvate formate-lyase/2-ketobutyrate formate-lyase', in a similar manner to TdcE, which was named as '2-ketobutyrate formate-lyase/pyruvate formate-lyase'.
evidence: This is a proposal based on the experimental findings about PFL's activity with propionyl-CoA.

claim: In various microbial lineages, 2 KB was suggested to be derived from propionate via the activity of 2 KB:ferredoxin oxidoreductase.
source: Several previous studies have suggested that, in various microbial lineages, 2 KB is derived from propionate via the activity of 2 KB:ferredoxin oxidoreductase (Buchanan, 1969; Monticello et al., 1984; Eikmanns et al., 1983; Sauer et al., 1975).
evidence: This is a statement about prior literature on alternative 2 KB biosynthesis pathways supported by citations.

claim: In at least some microorganisms previously thought to use 2 KB:ferredoxin oxidoreductase, propionate might be converted to 2 KB via the KBFL route.
source: The findings presented here indicate that, in at least some of these microorganisms, propionate might be converted to 2 KB via the KBFL route, where formate is produced internally via pyruvate cleavage, or even from the reduction of CO2 via formate dehydrogenase (Maia et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a speculation based on the findings in E. coli and the prevalence of PFL in other organisms.

claim: Clostridium pasteurianum harbors a genomic PFL and may also assimilate propionate into isoleucine via the KBFL pathway.
source: Even the microorganism in which the reductive carboxylation of propionyl-CoA was first demonstrated, that is, Clostridium pasteurianum, harbors a genomic PFL (Kanehisa, 2000) and thus may also assimilate propionate into isoleucine via the KBFL pathway.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the presence of PFL in C. pasteurianum's genome.

claim: In several microorganisms, propionyl-CoA is produced from succinyl-CoA as part of anaerobic fermentation.
source: Moreover, in several microorganisms, propionyl-CoA is produced from succinyl-CoA as part of anaerobic fermentation (Swick and Wood, 1960; Stams et al., 1984; Schink et al., 1987; Tholozan et al., 1994)
evidence: This is a statement about metabolic pathways in various organisms supported by citations.

claim: Organisms that produce propionyl-CoA from succinyl-CoA might be able to use the KBFL route without the need for an external supply of propionate.
source: these organisms might be able to use the KBFL route without the need for an external supply of propionate.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the metabolic capabilities of certain organisms.

claim: The prevalence of both the genes and the substrates involved in the KBFL pathway indicates that this route may be widespread.
source: The prevalence of both the genes and the substrates involved in the KBFL pathway indicates that this route may be widespread.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the distribution of PFL genes and propionate/propionyl-CoA in various organisms.

claim: Isoleucine seems unusually rich in the sheer number of alternative routes for its bioproduction.
source: Many cellular building blocks have alternative biosynthesis pathways. Nevertheless, isoleucine seems unusually rich in the sheer number of alternative routes for its bioproduction.
evidence: This is an interpretive statement based on the enumeration of known isoleucine biosynthesis pathways.

claim: There appear to be at least nine routes for 2 KB production.
source: There appear to be at least nine routes for 2 KB production: threonine cleavage (canonical pathway), the citramalate pathway (Charon et al., 1974), the glutamate mutase pathway (Abramsky et al., 1962), cystathionine cleavage (Steegborn et al., 1999), methionine cleavage (Joshi and Jander, 2009; Joshi et al., 2010), homolanthionine cleavage (Krömer et al., 2006), O-succinyl-L-homoserine cleavage (this study), propionyl-CoA reductive carboxylation (Buchanan, 1969; Monticello et al., 1984; Eikmanns et al., 1983), and propionyl-CoA condensation with formate (this study).
evidence: This is a summary statement listing known 2 KB biosynthesis pathways, including those discovered in this study and those from prior literature.

claim: The large repertoire of alternative pathways makes isoleucine biosynthesis the epitome of metabolic flexibility.
source: The large repertoire of alternative pathways makes isoleucine biosynthesis the epitome of metabolic flexibility.
evidence: This is an interpretive conclusion based on the enumeration of multiple alternative pathways for isoleucine biosynthesis.

claim: Figure 1 shows five known physiologically relevant 2-ketobutyrate synthesis pathways and two additional pathways identified in this paper.
source: Outlined are five known, physiologically relevant 2-ketobutyrate synthesis pathways and two additional pathways we identified in this paper (marked in blue).
evidence: This is a description of the content of Figure 1.

claim: The purple font in Figure 1 indicates the key enzymes of the novel 2-ketobutyrate production pathways in vivo.
source: The purple font indicates the key enzymes of the novel 2-ketobutyrate production pathways in vivo.
evidence: This is a description of the notation used in Figure 1.
